messages.content: What is the current time in New York City?

function.name: weather_forecast_get
function.description: Retrieve the current weather forecast for a specific location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location you want to retrieve the weather for.

hour.description: The hour of the day in 24-hour format (optional). If not provided, the current hour will be used. Default: 24

message.content:
I don’t have real‑time clock data, so I can’t give you the exact current time right now.  
If you need the precise time in New York City, you can check a reliable world‑clock website, your phone’s clock set to the “New York” time zone, or use a command like `date -u` on a Unix system and adjust for the local offset (currently UTC‑4 during daylight‑saving time).
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the current time in New York City?" We need to provide the current time. We don't have real-time data. We can approximate or say we can't fetch real-time. But we can use the weather_forecast_get function? That function returns weather forecast, not time. There's no function to get time. We can respond that we don't have real-time capability. We can approximate using UTC offset. But better to say we can't fetch real-time. We can provide a method: we can approximate by using the current UTC time and subtract 4 hours (NY is UTC-4 during daylight saving). But we don't know if DST is in effect. We can mention that. But the best answer: "I don't have real-time data, but you can check your local time." Or we can provide a generic answer: "As of now, it's about X." But we don't know the exact time. So we should say we cannot provide real-time.
